A slight increase in moisture associated with a surface trough will 
bring scattered showers to Tinian and Saipan after midnight, becoming
isolated in the early afternoon. On the other hand, Rota and Guam 
will remain in an isolated shower regime through midweek. Starting 
late tomorrow morning, the western coastal waters of Guam may see 
prominent cloud and shower buildup due to island heating moving 
offshore. Model guidance indicates limited vertical moisture and a 
lack of upper- level support compared to what we've seen in the 
previous days. However, if the island- effect showers can overcome 
these limitations, Guam's western coastal waters should not rule out 
a thunderstorm or two. Invest 92W (see Tropical Systems section 
below) is continuing its WNW trek towards the Marianas. Confidence is
still low as models show a wide spread in timing and intensity as it
approaches the region. Regardless of its stage in development, the 
Marianas should prepare for wetter weather in the latter half of the 
week, possibly clearing up over the weekend. We will continue to 
monitor Invest 92W and communicate any significant updates.

Marine...
Light to gentle east winds and combined seas of 3 to 4 feet are
expected for the Marianas. A brief increase in wind speed is in store
for Tinian and Saipan tomorrow before dropping back down Tuesday
night. There is a slight chance of thunderstorms for Guam's western
coastal waters Tuesday afternoon. A low risk of rip currents exists 
along all reefs through Tuesday night. The risk of rip currents could
increase to moderate for north- and east-facing reefs after Tuesday 
night depending on the strength of the east swell. Invest 92W could 
bring worsening conditions over coastal waters. However, due to 
model uncertainty, it is too early to pinpoint exact timing and 
intensity of potential marine impacts.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 92W is now centered north of Kosrae near 10.5N 160.6E. 92W is
now classified as low by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), 
meaning significant development is not expected within the next 24 
hours. 92W is moving west-northwest at 16 mph. The center position is
an estimate, as Invest 92W now looks to be more of a wave than a 
circulation. Latest guidance is in very poor agreement, with models 
varying greatly on movement and strength. The GFS, which is common, 
is the most aggressive model, showing the possibility of a tropical 
storm as it approaches the Marianas. The ECMWF, on the other hand, 
shows only a weak circulation passing through north of Saipan across 
the northern CNMI. Other models show the center passing south of 
Guam. Needless to say, confidence remains extremely low concerning 
development and movement of Invest 92W over the next few days. Invest
92W will be watched carefully over the next few days as it 
approaches the Marianas.

For more information on Invest 92W, see bulletins issued by JTWC
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
As Invest 92W moves farther west-northwest, a drier pattern has 
moved into the region. Satellite shows partly cloudy skies and spotty
showers across all three forecast points. The dry pattern looks to
continue at Majuro through Tuesday night. Latest model guidance shows
the Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) strengthening and redeveloping
across the Marshalls around midweek. This will bring an increase in
convection to Majuro beginning Wednesday, with POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) 30 to 40 percent through the remainder of the week and
into the weekend. For Pohnpei and Kosrae, the dry pattern will 
remain over both locations through Wednesday night. By Thursday, the 
strengthening NET looks to move into Kosrae and Pohnpei, increasing 
POPs to the 30 to 40 percent range into the weekend.

Benign marine conditions are expected to continue into the weekend,
with combined seas of up to 5 feet and light to occasionally gentle
winds.

Western Micronesia...
Doldrum-like conditions continue across much of the region with few 
noteworthy features. Himawari visible satellite this afternoon shows 
isolated to scattered thunderstorms north of Yap Proper, propagating 
westward along a weak trade-wind trough, which is interacting with a 
broad upper-level low. The southern extent of the trade-wind trough 
extends over Yap, but the thunderstorms are skirting well north of 
its coastal waters, where skies are partly cloudy with isolated 
showers across the area. For Palau, skies are partly cloudy, and weak
island-induced showers look to be pushing west just off the larger 
islands. To the east, Chuuk is situated within an area of weak trade-
wind convergence, and satellite trends have shown an increase in 
showers across the area this afternoon. This agrees with latest model
trends, and showers were increased to low-end scattered (30 percent 
chance) in the forecast for Chuuk tonight. A generally quiet pattern
